paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus meets people right where they are, and He doesn't flinch. A tired man sits at a well and asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, even though "Jews do not associate with Samaritans" (John 4:9). He tells her the whole truth about her life, and He doesn't push her away (John 4:17-18). Then He tells her plainly, "I who speak to you am He" (John 4:26).

She asked WHERE to worship, and Jesus answered HOW. He says "the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him" (John 4:23). Think about that, baker. The Father is out looking for worshipers, and He isn't checking the address. And the water Jesus gives isn't a refill, because it becomes "a fount of water springing up to eternal life" (John 4:14).

Then look at what happens next. The woman leaves her jar and tells her town what she found, and many believe because of her words (John 4:39). Then they hear Jesus for themselves and say, "this man truly is the Savior of the world" (John 4:42). So you don't need to be the expert, friend. Just point people to Jesus, like I point bakers to the Word, and let Him do the rest.
